scope: Broad TOPA sweep for exact decision-safe truncation/compression mechanisms and barriers relevant to unrestricted SAT/TRUMP.
captain_summary: The literature strongly supports certified local deletion and structured/parameterized compression, but it does not supply a universal polynomial-size exact SAT state. The missing theorem is guaranteed polynomial progress to a polynomial-time terminal class on every 3-CNF.

verified_lines.title: Effective Preprocessing in SAT through Variable and Clause Elimination
verified_lines.finding: Davis-Putnam variable elimination, combined with bounded growth and subsumption, provides satisfiability-equivalent preprocessing.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Safe variable deletion is real, but bounding local resolvent growth is a policy restriction, not a universal progress theorem.

verified_lines.title: Blocked Clause Elimination
verified_lines.finding: Blocked clauses can be deleted without changing satisfiability; the rule is local and practical.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: A canonical example of polynomially checkable decision-safe tail deletion.

verified_lines.title: Local Redundancy in SAT: Generalizations of Blocked Clauses
verified_lines.finding: Semantic blocking is the most general local redundancy property; broader local rules exist beyond ordinary BCE.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: R34 can search for one stronger local proof-carrying rule, but locality itself does not imply completeness on all CNFs.

verified_lines.title: Lean clause-sets: generalizations of minimally unsatisfiable clause-sets
verified_lines.finding: Autarky systems delete clauses that cannot contribute to unsatisfiability proofs and naturally leave lean kernels where the selected autarky system has no further deletion.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Direct conceptual precedent for R33: certified deletion may halt on a nontrivial lean core.

verified_lines.title: Infeasibility of instance compression and succinct PCPs for NP
verified_lines.finding: Strong generic OR-SAT compression to polynomial output length would have major complexity consequences, including NP in coNP/poly / PH collapse formulations in the paper's framework.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Do not assume a universal polynomial exact compression theorem as a preprocessing primitive; proving one is essentially major complexity progress.

verified_lines.title: On Compiling Structured CNFs to OBDDs
verified_lines.finding: Some structured CNF classes have polynomial OBDD size, while bounded-degree expander-based CNFs require exponential OBDD size.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: A representation can be polynomial on special structure and exponentially large on other sparse formulas; structural certification must be explicit.

verified_lines.title: Efficient Computation of Representative Families with Applications in Parameterized and Exact Algorithms
verified_lines.finding: Representative families safely discard states while preserving extension possibilities under explicit matroid/parameter conditions.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: A strong model for certified decision-safe table truncation, but its size guarantee depends on structural parameters and is not automatically polynomial for unrestricted SAT.

verified_lines.title: Sparsification / k-SAT complexity line
verified_lines.finding: k-SAT can be decomposed into a subexponential number of sparse instances; sparse formulas remain central hard objects rather than becoming trivially polynomial.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Clause-count reduction alone is not the missing invariant; R33 intentionally includes sparse Tseitin controls.

verified_lines.title: SAT backdoor parameterization literature
verified_lines.finding: A small backdoor can reduce a formula to a tractable residual class, but detecting or guaranteeing a universally polynomially bounded backdoor is a separate obligation.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Probe backdoor size only as a structural parameter; FPT in k does not imply P unless k is itself provably O(log n) or otherwise yields polynomial total cost under the fixed policy.

verified_lines.title: DRAT/LPR/propagation-redundancy proof logging line
verified_lines.finding: Many strong preprocessing transformations can be accompanied by independently checkable proof objects; supplied witnesses can move expensive semantic trust into polynomial checking even when discovery is harder.
verified_lines.TRUMP_use: Every new safe-reduction rule should emit a certificate and keep discovery cost separate from verification cost.

recommended_experimental_law: ATTACK THE FIRST CERTIFIED-REDUCTION FIXPOINT, PRESERVE IT, THEN ADD AT MOST ONE NEW PRE-REGISTERED POLYNOMIAL CHECKABLE RULE THAT TARGETS THE SEALED FAILURE.
